statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 15% (low) after a fourth observed hour of the CME reopen, with NQZ26 at 31,197.25, up 0.44% on 22.5k contracts, having absorbed a 24-point pullback and extended to a fresh 31,203.00 session high. Stress eases to 62% (elevated) as Brent 101.67 and WTI 90.23 both sit at session lows despite the Strait of Hormuz remaining declared closed, while the 10-year at 5.2939% keeps the rates tension in place.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. The narrow danger window is drawn across the 13:00-15:00Z block on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the US cash open, the S&P Global services and composite finals at 13:45Z and the September ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z, where the published Tail path peaks at 16% on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this state.
headline: Tail edges to 15% as a fourth reopen hour absorbs a 24-point pullback and extends to a new high, while crude at session lows keeps Stress easing to 62%
body:
The CME equity-index reopen is now roughly three and a half hours old and it has produced an orderly, thin bid rather than a price path worth protecting against. NQZ26 prints 31,197.25, up 135.50 points or 0.44% on a 31,061.75 prior close, with volume building steadily through the session from roughly 7,900 contracts three hours ago to 13,092, then 18,920, and now 22,510. The session opened at 31,059.00 and has traded 31,059.00 to 31,203.00, a 144-point band worth about 0.46% of index value, with the last trade 5.75 points below the high.

The one genuinely new piece of structure this hour is a completed pullback-and-extension sequence. A high printed at 31,194.50, met a retracement of roughly 24 points, and that retracement was absorbed before price extended to a fresh 31,203.00 high. A shallow pullback followed by repeated extension is precisely the amplifier the contract names, and it is why Tail rises one point to 15% rather than holding. What restrains the increase is magnitude: a 24-point pullback is 0.08% of index value and the entire session band is 0.46%, so this is low-energy drift in a holiday-thinned book rather than a persistent one-way path. Tail at 15% stays deep inside the low band and maps to EA_ON and green. The dominant mode remains normal, because a 0.46% overnight range is not a trend however efficiently it was travelled.

Depth is the honest reason the published path keeps any premium at all tonight. Mainland China is closed from 1 to 7 October for the National Day holiday and reopens on 8 October, the Korea Stock Exchange is closed for National Day on 5 October, and Hong Kong trades without Stock Connect flows in either direction. Price discovery is therefore unusually offshore-driven, which both thins the book an extension would have to overcome and raises the risk that any headline in these hours is priced offshore first.

Cross-asset evidence argues the other way and is the reason Stress eases rather than firms. Iran's parliament speaker has kept the Strait of Hormuz declared closed on seven conditions, with transit reported at a small fraction of normal traffic and war-risk premiums at many multiples of pre-crisis levels, and crude has gone down anyway: Brent is 101.67, off 1.02% against a 102.72 prior close and sitting at its 101.64 session low, and WTI is 90.23, off 0.97% and likewise at its 90.21 low. Both crudes making session lows against a declared closure is a clear statement that geopolitical risk is not currently transmitting into the index. Aggregated reporting on Gulf flow recovery remains internally contradictory, so the published assessment leans on the verified price rather than on either flow figure.

The standing constraint on this index is rates, not geopolitics. Friday's September payroll report missed badly at 29,000 against a consensus above 80,000, with July and August revisions totalling a loss of about 60,000, unemployment up to 4.2% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% on the month and 3.0% on the year. Yields fell on the print and then reversed higher, closing above Thursday's levels: the 10-year at 5.2939%, up 5.99 basis points and at its highest in more than two decades, the 2-year at 4.8414% and the 30-year at 5.6448%, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 4.78%, 5.24% and 5.61% as of 1 October. The soft labour print did cut near-term tightening expectations sharply, with October hike odds falling to roughly a sixth from around a third a week earlier while a December move stays priced, and the Nasdaq-100 still closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00%, with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31. A record close against a two-decade-high long yield is what holds Stress at 62%, inside the elevated band, while Tail sits at 15%: an expensive, difficult environment that has so far kept mean-reverting.

Confidence is 85%, unchanged. The evidence base is strong where it matters most: two independent verified futures reads including level, session range and volume, with the fresher one timestamped 01:18Z, real-time Brent and WTI, H.15 constant-maturity yields, the complete payroll actuals and revisions with Friday's yield closes, the verified August ISM Services report including its 47.8 employment and 72.6 prices sub-indices, the confirmed Asian holiday calendar, and the week's US event calendar cross-checked against two sources. Offsetting deductions apply and are the reason Confidence does not rise: VIX is a Friday cash close rather than a live read, cash Treasuries are shut overnight so the yield tension cannot be confirmed live, two intended sources for the rate-expectation figures returned HTTP 403 bot-blocks so that strand rests on aggregated reporting rather than a page read end to end, the Hormuz flow reporting is internally contradictory, and the shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection time with a partial collection status, roughly six days stale against the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was treated as unavailable and no breadth, megacap or semiconductor cross-check was folded in.

The published path holds Tail at 15% through the Tokyo handoff, where the thin book remains the main channel for unopposed extension, then decays to a 13% to 14% range as the Asian book is expected to mature and establish two-way trade. It ticks to 14% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to the 12% floor through the European morning, and rises into the US session: 15% for the 13:00Z hour containing the cash open and the S&P Global finals, and a 16% session peak for the 14:00Z hour carrying September ISM Services, whose consensus is 55.0 against a 55.4 August print and whose employment component carries extra weight after a 29,000 payroll gain. Both increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not assertions that opening continuation has already been observed. The path then decays through the afternoon, ticks to 14% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close and the maintenance halt, and settles at the 12% floor across the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour stays in the low band and maps to EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history. Tail was held at 3% from 01:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Tail then rose to 12% in the 22:00Z slot once the reopen had been observed, to 13% at 23:00Z as the drift extended, and to 14% at 00:00Z on 5 October. Stress climbed from 74% at 01:00Z to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, then eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings into the 14:00Z trough as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and settled at 66%, 65% and 64% across the three reopen hours. Confidence ran a narrow 83% to 88% band, peaking in the European and early US hours when verified evidence was densest and easing into the thin weekend and reopen hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour contains a fourth observed hour of the reopen, which has absorbed a 24-point pullback from 31,194.50 and extended to a fresh 31,203.00 high, lifting the gap to 0.44% on 22.5k contracts, so Tail edges to 15% while Stress eases to 62% on Brent and WTI both printing session lows. Tail holds 15% through the Tokyo handoff, where a book missing mainland China and Korea remains the main channel for unopposed extension, then decays to a 13% to 14% range as the Asian session is expected to mature into two-way trade. It ticks to 14% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to the 12% floor through the European morning, and rises to 15% and a 16% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours carrying the US cash open, the S&P Global services finals and September ISM Services at a 55.0 consensus. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances rather than observed structure. The path decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 14% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close and maintenance halt, and settles at the 12% floor across the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour remains in the low band and maps to EA_ON, with Stress tracking a 60% to 66% range and Confidence an 82% to 86% range.
